title: feat(spec,plugin-security,lint): sharing.controlledByParent.ownerMayEdit — a detail row's owner updates it with read on the master
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb5W448EqsD4LxfjvHNdpyC4)_
Fixes #25760

Clause-②: yes (widening) — a detail row's owner now passes the master-detail write gate with READ on the master, on an object that declares the opt-in; everyone else, and every other shape of write, still needs master EDIT. The default is unchanged.
Metadata-protocol: added (`ObjectSchema.sharing.controlledByParent.ownerMayEdit`, a per-object opt-in read only under `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'`)
Ruling-ref: 6398566164 (letter 1)

## What changes

ADR-0055 §3 had one rule for every write of a `controlled_by_parent` detail: EDIT access to the master record. Salesforce's Activities under OWD = Controlled by Parent let the owner of an activity edit it while merely reading its account; the platform could not express that, and an authored `owner_id == current_user.id` update policy on the detail could not either, because the detail's own policies compose AND with the master gate (step 2.7 then 2.8), so such a policy only narrowed the master's editors.

- **Spec** (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`, `object.form.ts`, liveness ledger, generated authorable surface). `ObjectSchema` gains `sharing: { controlledByParent: { ownerMayEdit: boolean } }`, both blocks closed (`strictObject`, with guidance for the near-miss spellings). `ownerMayEdit: true` on an object that is not a `sharingModel: 'controlled_by_parent'` detail is refused at parse, one `custom` issue at `sharing.controlledByParent.ownerMayEdit`, with the prescription. The reader `controlledByParentOwnerMayEdit(schema)` (`@objectstack/spec/data`) answers `true` only for the parsed literal and fails closed on every other shape.
- **Gate** (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts`, `security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts`, `security-plugin.ts`). `CbpRelation` carries `ownerMayEdit`, resolved on the same registered schema the relation came from, and only when that schema carries the `owner_id` column (the registry's injected per-record owner under `ownership: 'user'`, the default). In `assertControlledByParentWrite`, before the §3 chain walk, a by-id `update` on an opted-in detail by the caller whose `userId` equals the stored row's `owner_id` is admitted when the caller can READ the master row, asked of the read door under the caller's own context (`readRowById` through `readUnlessRefused`, the same probe the by-id pre-image gate uses; a hidden row and a declared refusal are one answer, a store fault propagates). A body that re-points the master reference still asks EDIT on the master it names. `ISecurityService.checkControlledByParentWrite` answers the same way, since it runs the same check.
- **Lint** (`packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts`, `index.ts`). New advisory arm `security-controlled-by-parent-owner-policy-without-opt-in` (warning): an `update` or `all` row-level policy whose `using` or `check` keys a field on the caller (`FIELD == current_user.id`, either operand order, the SQL `=` spelling the compiler bridges, `record.FIELD` too) on a `controlled_by_parent` detail that has not declared the opt-in. Judged by shape on the canonical CEL parse; a predicate that does not parse is the parse rule's. `os explain` carries the entry. `warning`, not `error`, because `validateSecurityPosture` also runs at the runtime publish doors, where an `error` refuses the write, and a narrowing can be meant.
- **ADR-0055** amended in place (status line, §3 rule line, a final Amendment section: ruling, gap, what the opt-in does, out of scope, fail-closed boundaries, unchanged). Governed surface, Tier H.

## Scope: `update` only — stated as the ruling asks

The ruling names `update`. This PR admits the owner on a **by-id update** and nothing else:

- **insert**: no stored row to own; the master is still asked for EDIT.
- **delete**: not the ruled verb; still asked for EDIT on the master.
- **predicate update** (`multi: true`): judges every master of the rows it selects and has no single row whose owner could be asked; unchanged.
- **delegated write** (on-behalf-of): keeps the master-edit rule on both passes, as ADR-0090 D10 keeps both floors for every other relief.
- A row with no owner admits nobody; an opt-in on a detail whose schema has no `owner_id` column (`ownership` other than `'user'`) is inert and reported once per object at `warn` by the relation resolver (the parse cannot refuse that half: the injected-column plan lives in a module that imports `object.zod.ts`).

Insert and delete can be added later under the same key if the maintainer rules so; nothing here forecloses it.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

### 改了什么

给 `controlled_by_parent`(访问随主记录)的从对象加了一个按对象声明的开关 `sharing.controlledByParent.ownerMayEdit: true`。打开后,从记录的**所有者**(`owner_id` 是自己)只要能**读**主记录,就能按 id 修改自己这条从记录;其他人、以及新增/删除/按条件批量改/代办写入,仍然要求对主记录有**编辑**权。不开这个开关,一切照旧。`os lint` 新增一条提示:在没开开关的从对象上写了 `owner_id == current_user.id` 的更新策略,会提醒作者这条策略永远放不进所有者。ADR-0055 §3 同步修订。

### 为什么改

裁决 6398566164(第 1 条)。对应 Salesforce 的"活动随父记录控制,但活动所有者始终能编辑自己的活动"这一常见业务形态:销售能看客户、不能改客户,但要能改自己名下挂在客户上的任务/义务。原来平台表达不了,作者自己写行级策略也无效(策略只会收窄,不会放宽主记录门)。

### 风险与代价(含回滚)

- 放宽只在三件事同时成立时发生:对象显式声明了开关、调用者就是该行的 `owner_id`、调用者能读主记录。默认值不变,存量对象不受影响。
- 守住的边界都有测试钉住:非所有者、无所有者的行、读不到主记录的所有者、新增、删除、批量改、代办写、把行挪到另一个主记录下,全部仍被主记录门拒绝。
- 回滚:删除对象上的这一个键即可恢复原行为;代码层面整条逻辑是写门里一个独立的、先于原链路的分支,去掉分支即回到 §3 原规则。
- 成本:一次 `sys_`-级读探针(读主记录)只在上述三件事成立时才发生。

### 席位意见

(留空)

### 你要做的

1. 审阅 `docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md` 的修订段落(受管面,Tier H),确认"只放宽按 id 更新、不含新增/删除"的范围与裁决一致。
2. 批准后由席位落地;若希望新增/删除也纳入开关,请在卡上追加裁决,本 PR 不预设。

## Acceptance notes

- Owner = the platform's injected per-record owner `owner_id` (the sharing service's `OWNER_FIELD`, the "My records" scope), not `created_by`: the ruling says "the detail row's own owner", and the platform has one owner concept.
- The master READ probe runs under the caller's own context through the engine's read door, so it is the answer a direct read of the master gives (object grant, row-level and sharing scope, and the chain for a master that is itself a detail). For a detail whose master the caller cannot read, the by-id pre-image already answers not-found before the gate; the suite pins that refusal too.
- The detail's own object-level `update` grant and its own row-level policies (step 2.7) run before the leg, unchanged; an authored `owner_id == current_user.id` policy on an opted-in detail now decides as authored.
- The lint test's structural meta-guard (#5017) gained the new reads (`ps.rowLevelSecurity`, a `policy` receiver against `PermissionSetSchema.rowLevelSecurity[]`, the CEL AST receivers excused by name) and the push-site count moved 17 → 18 with a corpus fixture.
- Out of scope, noted not filed: `content/docs/permissions/*.mdx` do not yet mention the opt-in (the generated spec docs do, through the key's describe); the owner-column half of the opt-in is reported at runtime rather than refused at parse (documented in the ADR amendment and the gate).

## Verification

Head `dece7114`. Local verification, all under the shared verify lock where it is a build or a suite (the three affected packages, their dependency closure built first with `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-security^...' --filter '@objectstack/lint^...' build`, exit 0):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — Test Files 722 passed | 1 skipped (723), Tests 21899 passed | 1 skipped | 1 todo. `typecheck` exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test` — Test Files 224 passed (224), Tests 4700 passed | 45 skipped. `typecheck` exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` — Test Files 164 passed (164), Tests 7363 passed. `typecheck` exit 0.
- The new suites on their own: spec parse pins 14/14, plugin-security rig 17/17, lint arm + the posture suite + rule explanations 206/206.
- Ablation of the gate leg (`rel.ownerMayEdit` short-circuited to false, then the file restored from git): 4 of 17 rig pins red — the owner's admitted update, the delegated case's control, the body naming the row's own contract, and `checkControlledByParentWrite` answering `allow`; the 13 refusal pins stayed green, as they must (the leg adds no refusal of its own).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` exit 0 after regenerating the five artefacts it proved stale (api-surface, export-origins, docs, strictness-ledger counts, liveness counts); `check:liveness`, `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface`, `check:docs` exit 0.
- Derived gates (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 124 families for this change set): 122 run, every one exit 0, each exit code captured before any pipe; `--ran` reconciliation exit 0 with 0 UNRUN. 2 NOT MEASURED locally, both a recorded exit 3 (prerequisite: the whole farm's `dist/`, which this seat did not build): `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `pnpm check:i18n` — CI's check-runs are the verdict for those two.

Four pins outside the new suites moved with this diff, each a one-line or typed change, none a behaviour change: the two compose-stacks pins list `sharing` as the config object it is; the lint barrel-export pin wants the rule id on one line; the #5017 meta-guard table gained the arm's reads.
